correctness.rationale: With orientation σ and W=U−V of fixed nonzero sign, division by theta-dot gives ds/dθ=2s(1−s)U/(sU−V). On each s-side z=log|s/(1−s)| has ∂z[dz/dθ]=−2s(1−s)U²/(sU−V)²; integrating a full oriented angular revolution gives derivative of the z-Poincare map everywhere strictly above/below 1, so at most one off-circle zero per side and hyperbolicity. At s=1 write q=s−1, A=−2U/W, h=e^{∫A}; expansion q'=Aq+(A+A²/2)q² yields at M=h(2πσ)=1 quadratic return coefficient K=(1/2)∫_0^{2πσ}A²h, sign σ and nonzero since U not identically zero. Neutral P_z−z has boundary limit zero and strict monotonicity, excluding finite z fixed points; first-return parabolic recurrence on attracting side gives n q_n→−1/K. Exact trigonometric integrations and strict inequalities prove both sharp examples without orbit numerics.
